title: Expression Machine: Variables and Rules
subject: math
developmentNotes: Students often treat a variable as a label or concatenate numbers instead of applying a rule. Keep the input-output relationship visible before introducing symbolic notation.
learningObjective: Students will evaluate one-variable expressions by substituting a value, following operation order, and explaining each step as a machine rule.
essentialQuestion: How can a rule turn an unknown input into a predictable output?

vocabularyTerms.definition: a letter or symbol that can stand for a number
numbers, variables, and operations without an equals sign
a number that multiplies a variable
a number that stays fixed in an expression
find the value of an expression when the variable is known

learningObjective: Students will evaluate one-variable expressions by substituting a value, following operation order, and explaining each step as a machine rule.
successCriteria: I can explain what the variable represents.
I can substitute a value without losing the operation.
I can follow the expression rule in order.
I can debug a wrong output and explain the correction.

knowledge: A variable is a number placeholder, not a label.
Multiplication and addition rules can be represented by an expression.
capability: Build and test an input-output table.
reasoning: Explain why the order of operations changes the output.
Use an expected output to find a broken step.
retention: Retrieve the substitute-then-operate process after a delay.
transfer: Use an expression to model a changed real-world rule.

phaseModules.title: Enter the expression machine
phaseModules.studentAction: Predict the output of a machine that multiplies an input by 3 and adds 2.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can name the input, rule, and output.

phaseModules.title: Watch the rule run
phaseModules.studentAction: Follow n = 4 through 3n + 2: substitute 4, multiply to get 12, then add 2 to get 14.
phaseModules.visualSupport: Expression machine diagram with input, multiply, add, and output.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can point to each step instead of jumping to the final number.

phaseModules.title: Separate the parts
phaseModules.studentAction: Sort cards into variable, coefficient, operation, and constant, then explain what each part does.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can identify every job in the expression.

phaseModules.title: Run the machine
phaseModules.studentAction: Test several inputs in 3n + 2 and record each output in an input-output table.
phaseModules.successCheck: My table follows the same rule for every input.

phaseModules.title: Debug a broken output
phaseModules.studentAction: Compare a student answer of 3 + 4 + 2 with the machine rule and explain which operation was skipped.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can name the error and connect it to the rule.

phaseModules.title: Pass the checkpoint
phaseModules.studentAction: Evaluate new expressions, explain one step, and correct one deliberately broken solution without final-answer help.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can prove the output with a visible chain of steps.

phaseModules.title: Store the process
phaseModules.studentAction: After a delay, retrieve the sequence: substitute, multiply or divide, then add or subtract as the rule says.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can use the process without looking at the model.

phaseModules.title: Design a new rule
phaseModules.studentAction: Model a real situation such as a 4-dollar entry fee plus 2 dollars per game, then evaluate it for a chosen number of games.
phaseModules.successCheck: I can connect each part of my expression to the situation.

phaseModules.title: Choose the next move
phaseModules.studentAction: Choose variable meaning, substitution, operation order, or debugging as your next tutor route based on the exact error.
phaseModules.successCheck: My next step matches the evidence from my work.

proofTasks.prompt: State the three-step process for evaluating an expression.
Explain what the variable and coefficient mean in 3n + 2.
Evaluate 4n + 1 when n = 3 and show the steps.
After a delay, evaluate a new expression without reopening the model.
Write an expression for a changed real-world fee rule and evaluate it.

feedbackRules.result: The learner treats the variable as a name instead of a number placeholder.
feedbackRules.hint: Ask what number the variable stands for in this input.

feedbackRules.result: The learner adds before multiplying or skips a rule step.
feedbackRules.hint: Trace the machine one box at a time and write the intermediate output.

feedbackRules.result: The learner substitutes a value but loses the coefficient operation.
feedbackRules.hint: Keep the multiplication symbol visible before calculating.

feedbackRules.result: The learner gives an answer without a rule or intermediate step.
feedbackRules.hint: Ask which machine box proves the next number.

reteachPaths.trigger: The learner drops a symbol or skips a machine step.
reteachPaths.action: Return to a two-box machine with small inputs, keep the coefficient visible, and narrate each intermediate output.

prerequisiteRepairPaths.trigger: The learner cannot use multiplication or addition reliably.
prerequisiteRepairPaths.action: Repair the needed operation with a concrete array or number line before evaluating the expression.

challengePaths.trigger: The learner evaluates current-context expressions independently.
challengePaths.action: Design two different fee or scoring rules, compare their outputs, and explain which rule grows faster.

visual.title: Expression machine
visual.caption: Input -> multiply by 3 -> add 2 -> output
visual.altText: A labeled machine shows an input n moving through multiply by 3 and add 2 to produce an output.

visualSupports.title: Expression machine mission board
visualSupports.description: A neon classroom-safe machine with input, multiply, add, and output boxes.
visualSupports.prompt: Create a high-contrast Grade 6 math teaching diagram showing an input n moving through multiply by 3, add 2, and output. Include one worked example n=4 -> 14, short readable labels, no logos, no real children.
visualSupports.altText: Expression machine with input n, multiply by 3, add 2, and output 14.

visualSupports.title: Substitute then operate
visualSupports.description: Show 3n + 2 with n replaced by 4, then show 3 x 4 = 12 and 12 + 2 = 14.
visualSupports.prompt: Create a clean labeled step-by-step diagram for evaluating 3n + 2 when n=4. Use large labels, arrows, high contrast, and one intermediate result.
visualSupports.altText: Steps replace n with 4, multiply 3 by 4 to get 12, then add 2 to get 14.

visualSupports.title: Expression tutor repair card
visualSupports.description: Ask whether the error is variable meaning, substitution, operation order, or missing evidence.
visualSupports.prompt: Create a small tutor hint card with four labeled repair routes for a Grade 6 expression machine: variable, substitution, order, and proof. No tiny text.
visualSupports.altText: Tutor repair card with four routes: variable, substitution, order, and proof.

quiz.question: If n=4, what is 3n+2?
quiz.explanation: Substitute 4, multiply 3 x 4 to get 12, then add 2.

quiz.question: A learner evaluates 3n+2 with n=4 as 3+4+2. What step was lost?
quiz.correctAnswer: The coefficient 3 must multiply n before adding 2.
quiz.explanation: The coefficient is an operation, not a separate number to add.

quiz.question: What does n represent in 3n+2?
quiz.correctAnswer: The input number that the rule changes.
quiz.explanation: A variable stands for a number in the situation.

quiz.question: A game costs 4 dollars to enter plus 2 dollars per round. Write a rule and find the cost for 3 rounds.
quiz.explanation: The fixed fee is 4 and each round adds 2.

retrievalCheck.prompt: What is the first step when evaluating an expression with a known variable?
retrievalCheck.expectedAnswer: Substitute the known value for the variable.
retrievalCheck.feedbackIfMissed: Show the input card, replace the letter, and retry one small example.

memoryVaultItems.expectedAnswer: Substitute, follow the operations, and explain the output.
memoryVaultItems.failureAction: Show the labeled machine and schedule a next-day retry.
memoryVaultItems.successAction: Change the input and ask for the process again.

groupHomework.title: Rule designers lab
groupHomework.sharedOutcome: Design a fair game or snack rule, map it as an expression machine, and test three inputs.
groupHomework.individualAccountability: Each learner explains one part of the rule and debugs one test output.

accessibilityNotes: Provide text equivalents for every machine diagram.
Do not use color alone to identify machine steps.
Allow keyboard entry, oral explanation, or a paper input-output table.
ageFitNotes: Bridge Academy pacing uses a visible system model, short challenges, and independent explanation before transfer.

readability.supportNotes: Keep directions short, show one intermediate result, and define each symbol before using it.
